newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks seen plunging on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks seen plunging on IMF news.

text.p: Pakistani stocks finished up on Friday but are likely to take a plunge on Monday after an International Monetary Fund decision to suspend a standby loan to Pakistan, dealers said.
The IMF decision, announced hours after close of trading, is likely to keep foreign investors away from the market," said Jahanzeb Naseer, research head at Jardine Fleming Pakistan.
The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index rose 10.47 points, or 0.66 percent, to end at 1,592.75. Gainers led losers 158 to 93. Turnover fell to 36 million shares from 41 million on Thursday.
Askari Bank rose 0.90 to 29 rupees and Askari General Insurance 2.35 to 24.75. Nishat Mills rose 1.25 to 26.25 and Dewan Salman Fibre 0.85 to 39.15.
Hub Power Co rose 0.10 to 37.55, PTCL 0.40 to 30.55, Fauji Fertilizer 2.50 to 84 and ICI Pakistan 0.75 to 23.45.
